capabilities.description: Build one change in this repo: implement it, prove it, and close the issue that asked for it. Always repo-provided — nothing generic can know how this product is built.

operations.description: Make the change the issue asks for on a work branch, and push it. Where the context carries a port source this is a port, not a replay: adapt the change to the target line, because a port that needs adapting is a real change.

input.issue: object — the issue being worked, including the repo that holds it
input.line: string — the line to implement on, e.g. v17
input.port: object|null — the source line and commit when this is a port of an already-landed change

output.branch: string — the branch the work was pushed to
output.summary: string — what was changed, for the PR body

issue.title: Validation message ignores the current culture

operations.description: Run this repo's build, tests and sanity checks against the change, and report pass or fail with enough detail for the caller to act on a failure.

input.scope: string — optional narrowing, e.g. one test project

output.failures: array — one entry per failing check, with its output

operations.description: Told that a PR has landed, work out which issue it was for and close that issue only once EVERY target line has landed — one logical change lands N times at N moments. The caller passes the PR, not the issue, because how a PR references its issue and which lines are targets are both repo facts. MUST close explicitly: a `Closes #N` keyword does not cross repos. MUST tolerate an already-closed issue, and MUST report `closed: false` with the lines still outstanding rather than closing early.

input.landed: object — the PR that just landed: repo, pr_number, and its line
input.issue: object — optional, when the caller already knows which issue it was

output.issue: object — the issue this resolved to, so the caller can report it
output.waiting_on: array — target lines not yet landed; empty when closed is true

capabilities.description: Turn a release trigger into a shipped release for this repo: plan it, cut it, publish it, then put the line's branches back in step. Always repo-provided — version sources and publish targets are product facts.

operations.description: Turn the trigger into release facts: which line, which version, and which units of work the release contains. Reads only; opens nothing.

input.trigger: object — the issue, label or dispatch that asked for a release

output.units: array — the changes included, for the changelog

operations.description: Branch, bump the version files, write the changelog, and open the release PR. Idempotent: re-running MUST return the existing release PR, never open a second.
Realize the release once its PR has landed: tag the commit, push the artifacts to their feed, and publish the release notes. MUST leave nothing half-published on failure.

input.merge_commit: string — the commit the release PR landed as

operations.description: Put the line's branches back in step after a release, so the next change starts from what actually shipped. The step manual releases most often forget.

input.line: string — the line that was just released

output.pr_number: integer|null — set when the sync needed a PR rather than a fast-forward

capabilities.description: Land an approved PR. Owns every piece of merge policy: the gates, the release-base skip, and the merge itself. A loop hands it a PR and reads an outcome; the loop never holds a branch name or a merge strategy. The gates are engine policy, so the framework default should fit every repo.

operations.description: Check every gate, then merge, or decline with the reason. Gates: the landing label is present, CI is green, the PR is mergeable, and its base is a live integration branch. Re-checks CI itself rather than trusting the caller's poll. Outcome is one of `merged`, `skipped:release-base`, `blocked:ci`, `blocked:conflict`, `blocked:changes-requested`, `blocked:wrong-base`, `blocked:no-label` — a fixed set the evals assert on, not an enforced envelope. Idempotent: an already-merged PR MUST report that merge, not attempt another.

input.pr: object — the PR to land, including its repo and number

output.outcome: string — one of the seven above
output.detail: string — the specific blocker, for the loop to comment

capabilities.description: This repo's branch model, and the only holder of it. The integration branches, the release base and the merge strategy are private: callers ask for an outcome, never for a value. Command-only — it answers no reads, and it reads the live-line set from `repo-meta` every time rather than caching it, because a new major adds a line without an engine change.

operations.description: Merge a PR using whichever strategy this repo's model calls for. The caller passes no strategy and learns none. Checking the base is membership of the live-line set, never equality with one branch.
Open a PR from a work branch onto the correct base for its line, choosing that base internally.
Create a work branch for a change, named to this repo's convention and rooted on the correct base for its line.

input.slug: string — a short kebab-case description of the work

capabilities.description: An isolated place to build and test one change: worktree, database, dependencies, credentials. Prepared and torn down by `ops-change`, never by a loop.

operations.description: Create the isolated workspace for a branch and leave it ready to build. Idempotent: an existing workspace for that branch MUST be reused, not duplicated.
Remove the workspace and everything it created, including any database or container. MUST succeed when there is nothing left to remove.

capabilities.description: Ambient facts about this repo and its family, as data. A data capability: the structure is the deliverable, so every action MUST return well-formed structured output rather than prose. Detection fills in what it can; a repo declares the rest.

operations.description: Name the repo the loop is working in, and the labels and defaults it runs by.

output.labels: object — the trigger labels this repo uses, by purpose

operations.description: Say which repo fills each of the four roles — `code` (required), `issues`, `releases` and `learnings`. An unspecified role resolves to `code`, so a single-repo project returns only `code`. `learnings` is not automatically `issues`: where issues are public and code is not, learnings follow the code.

List the live lines, say which is primary, and give the port order. None of it is derivable from version numbers or from the default branch, so a repo declares it: the primary line need not be the newest line or the default branch. Callers MUST read this rather than cache it, because a major-version cutover adds a line.

output.live: array — the lines currently taking work
output.primary: string — the line work starts on before being ported

capabilities.description: This repo's CI, read-only. Both actions are reads: nothing here starts, retries or cancels a build. The CI provider is internal — no caller learns which one this repo uses.

operations.description: Report the CI state of a PR: pending, green or red, and which checks produced that verdict.

output.checks: array — name and conclusion per check

operations.description: Return the failing part of a failing build's log, trimmed to what is needed to diagnose it rather than the whole run.

input.check: string — which check to read; omit for the first failing one

output.check: string — the check it came from

capabilities.description: Tell a human something happened, through whichever channel this repo uses. Infrastructure: callable from any layer, and never a gate — a failed notification MUST NOT fail the work it was reporting on.

operations.description: Send one notification to a human through whichever channel this repo uses. Idempotent per `key`: the same key twice MUST NOT produce a second message.

input.subject: string
input.key: string — a stable id for this notification, for de-duplication

example.subject: Landed PR #8890
example.body: The v17 line went green and merged. v18 port is still open.
